Question: Points \(P\) and \(Q\) are chosen uniformly and independently at random on sides \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{AC},\) respectively, of equilateral triangle \(\triangle ABC.\) Which of the following intervals contains the probability that the area of \(\triangle APQ\) is less than half the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)
Solution:
Only an interval is requested, so bounding the probability will suffice. Let
\[
x=\frac{AP}{AB},\qquad y=\frac{AQ}{AC},
\]
where \(0\le x,y\le1\), and write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\). Triangles \(APQ\) and \(ABQ\) have the same height to line \(AB\), while triangles \(ABQ\) and \(ABC\) have the same height to line \(AC\). Therefore
\[
[APQ]=x[ABQ],\qquad [ABQ]=y[ABC],
\]
so \([APQ]/[ABC]=xy\). These equalities also hold when either small triangle has zero area.

The independent uniform choices make \((x,y)\) uniform in the unit square, whose area is \(1\). Thus probabilities equal areas there. Let \(q\) be the probability of the complementary event \(xy\ge\tfrac12\), including equality.

If \(xy\ge\tfrac12\), both coordinates must be at least \(\tfrac12\), so this region lies in the square \([\tfrac12,1]^2\), of area \(\tfrac14\). However, the smaller square \([\tfrac12,\tfrac23]^2\) is excluded, since throughout it
\[
xy\le\frac49<\frac12.
\]
That excluded square has positive area \(\tfrac1{36}\), giving
\[
q\le\frac14-\frac1{36}=\frac29<\frac14.
\]
For a bound in the other direction, observe that throughout the unit square,
\[
xy=x+y-1+(1-x)(1-y)\ge x+y-1.
\]
Consequently every point with \(x+y\ge\tfrac32\) belongs to the complementary event. Those points form the upper-right corner triangle with perpendicular legs of length \(\tfrac12\), whose area is \(\tfrac18\). Hence \(q\ge\tfrac18\).

The desired probability is \(p=1-q\), so
\[
\frac18\le q<\frac14
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\frac34<p\le\frac78.
\]
This is choice \(\boxed{\mathrm{D}}\).
